content.title: About
content.content: Tortellini are small ring-shaped pasta filled with creamy cheese. This meatless version is served in a fragrant tomato sauce. The durum wheat dough gives a firm bite, while the cheese filling adds a mild, slightly tangy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortellini originate from Italy, especially the Emilia‑Romagna and Tuscany regions.
The name “tortellini” derives from the Italian “tortello,” meaning “little cake.”
Cheese fillings are often made from ricotta, Parmesan, and fresh herbs, making the dish vegetarian.
The tomato sauce typically includes ripe tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, and basil.
Tortellini freeze well; after thawing they retain their shape and taste.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides both dairy and plant protein, supporting tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese supplies calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Dairy in the filling delivers vitamin B12, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, which helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes and olive oil stimulate bile production, aiding fat absorption.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheese filling may contain lactose, causing discomfort for those who are intolerant.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy ingredients.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if needed.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The wheat dough contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the tortellini hot, drenched in tomato sauce. Top with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or a drizzle of olive oil. They pair well with a light salad or vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry tortellini in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked tortellini in sauce should be refrigerated and consumed within 3‑4 days. Frozen tortellini retain quality for up to 2 months.
